referees.quote: I recommend publication in Nature Communications. A few minor comments before publication include the following
the potential impact of the manuscript meets the high standards of Nature Communications, but I would like the authors to address the following questions before I can recommend it for publication.
the current presentation does not fully exclude a potentially important contribution from sublattice-symmetry breaking... the authors should provide a more explicit justification

note: First round is Version 0 in this file; there is no sign of a transfer from another journal, and no referee co-signs another's report. None of the three referees uses the scale terms, so all levels are inferred. R1 recommends publication and calls its points minor. R2 is positive and asks two questions; the only extra data it requests (a bare tDBLG comparison) is qualified with 'if possible', so I read it as minor revision. R3 gives no overall verdict. It asks for modeling to rule out sublattice symmetry breaking as an alternative to the central claim, plus lower-temperature D3 data, a device-variation discussion, a quantitative theory-experiment comparison and a figure fix. Because the requests include new analysis and possibly new measurements bearing on the central claim, I classed R3 as major revision. This is a borderline call: its tone is constructive ('I hope the comments below will help strengthen the paper') and the new data is requested 'if such measurements are available'. All three referees recommended publication in the second round.
